lessons.title: Checking dispatch containers
lessons.html:
Checking dispatch containers

Grain leaves the silo in trucks, trailers, rail trucks, shipping containers or bags. These are called dispatch containers. Before grain is loaded, the container must be checked and made ready. Grain is food for people and animals. A dirty container can spoil the whole load.

What to look for

  • Old grain and dirt: left-over grain, chaff, dust or mud. Old grain may have insects.
  • Insects: weevils, beetles, moths or their webs.
  • Strange smells: fuel, chemicals, fertiliser, dung, rotten food. Grain takes up smells.
  • Wet patches, rust or mould.
  • Holes and gaps in the floor, sides or doors, where grain can leak out or rain can get in.
  • Broken doors, locks or outlet slides.
  • Torn tarpaulins or missing ropes.
  • Signs of the last load. Ask the driver what was carried before. A truck that carried fertiliser, chemicals, coal or animals needs special cleaning or must be rejected.

Example

A truck arrives to load wheat for a mill. Nomsa climbs the ladder at the inspection platform and looks inside. She smells diesel and sees a wet patch in a corner. She tells her supervisor. The truck is sent to be cleaned and dried. If it had been loaded, the mill could have rejected the whole load.

Safety when checking

  • Engine off and handbrake on before you climb.
  • Use the inspection platform or a safe ladder. Do not climb the side of the truck.
  • Keep three points of contact on a ladder: two hands and one foot, or two feet and one hand.
  • Use a torch to see inside. Do not climb into a closed container alone.

lessons.title: Cleaning and preparing containers for loading
lessons.html:
Cleaning and preparing for loading

Cleaning steps

  1. Sweep out all old grain, dust and dirt. Start at the front and work to the back or the outlet.
  2. Use a brush on corners and the edges of doors.
  3. Use compressed air or a blower where your site allows it. Wear safety glasses and a dust mask.
  4. If the container is wet, let it dry before loading. Grain loaded onto a wet floor will get mouldy.
  5. Put the sweepings into the waste bin, not back into a grain bin.

Preparing

  • Close and lock outlet slides and doors.
  • Cover small holes or gaps as your site procedure says, or report them. A truck with big holes must not be loaded.
  • Check the tarpaulin is ready to cover the load after loading.
  • For bags: check that bags are clean, the right type, and not torn.

Sign off

Many silos use a container inspection checklist. Tick each item, write the truck registration, date and time, and sign. Your supervisor or the client may also need to sign. If the container is rejected, write down why.

CheckOK?
Clean, no old grainYes / No
No insectsYes / No
No strange smellYes / No
DryYes / No
No holes, doors closeYes / No

Never

  • Never load a container that smells of chemicals or fuel.
  • Never sign the checklist without looking.
  • Never climb into a container while grain is loading.

Key points

  • Check for old grain, insects, smells, wet patches and holes.
  • Ask what the container carried last.
  • Sweep clean, let it dry, and close all outlets.
  • Fill in and sign the inspection checklist honestly.
  • Use the platform and keep three points of contact on ladders.
